key_insight: A single diffusion-based model can be made scale-adaptive to perform joint spatial and temporal super-resolution across varying upsampling factors, enabling one model to generalize to multiple spatial resolutions and frame rates.
problem_solved: Current joint spatiotemporal super-resolution models are typically tied to a fixed pair of spatial and temporal upscaling factors, forcing retraining for new resolutions or cadences and limiting transferability for climate and video applications.
method: Use a diffusion generative model trained for joint spatiotemporal super-resolution, modeling both spatial detail and temporal dynamics.
Introduce scale-adaptive conditioning/training so the same model accepts variable spatial and temporal SR factors (or conditioning vectors) at inference, removing the need for per-scale retraining.
Train with multi-scale examples and leverage progressive or multi-resolution synthesis to preserve fidelity across a range of upsampling ratios.
impact: Enables practitioners to deploy one flexible SR model across multiple spatial resolutions and frame rates, reducing engineering cost and improving applicability to climate datasets and diverse video sources.
visual_elements: Schematic: low-res spatiotemporal cube -> scale-adaptive diffusion model -> high-res spatiotemporal cube (showing both more pixels and frames).
Diagram: conditioning mechanism that takes arbitrary spatial/temporal scale inputs and routes them into the diffusion model.
Bar/line chart: performance (accuracy/quality) vs. upscaling factor comparing single-task models vs. the scale-adaptive model.
Use-case icons: climate maps, weather forecast timelines, and a single-model deployment box to convey transferability and reduced training burden.
paper_title: A Scale-Adaptive Framework for Joint Spatiotemporal Super-Resolution with Diffusion Models
paper_authors: Max Defez, Filippo Quarenghi, Mathieu Vrac, Stephan Mandt, Tom Beucler
